profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC21 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.

reading.body:
Equinix DC21 is a 39,665 square foot facility on Equinix's Ashburn campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, part of Data Center Alley. The operator publishes no power capacity, square footage density, or specific certifications for this building. DC2, described as representative of the campus's general specifications, offers N+1 power and cooling redundancy with a stated minimum cabinet density of 4 kVA, but these figures are not confirmed for DC21 itself.

Ashburn hosts the greatest published concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's DC1 and DC2 from the late 1990s. The region serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia as a state has 330 mapped data center facilities and 23 with published power capacity totaling 1,375 megawatts.

Without published megawatt capacity, DC21 cannot be ranked by power among Virginia's 23 disclosed facilities or evaluated for its contribution to AI scaling capacity. The building's role in the Ashburn campus, historically positioned as an internet exchange hub rather than a compute facility, and the absence of any published specifications for this specific site, mean its relevance to AI infrastructure depends on information Equinix has not disclosed.
